facts.text: Lake Barcroft was created when the Alexandria Water Company built a dam on Holmes Run in 1915, forming a 620‑million‑gallon reservoir.
In 1942 the dam was raised by five feet, expanding the lake to 800 million gallons and adding 24 gates for better water control.
After Hurricane Agnes in 1972 flooded the lake above the dam, the community rebuilt the damaged spillway and the lake remained dry for two years.
The Lake Barcroft Community Association, founded in the early 1950s, later became the Lake Barcroft Association that manages the lake and surrounding common grounds.
The lake’s name honors Dr. Barcroft, a 19th‑century mill owner who built his home on the site and helped establish the early community.
Lake Barcroft sits on 680 acres that were purchased for $1 million in 1949 and later sold to residents for $300,000 in 1970, turning the area into a planned residential community.
